content: The settings file is named prefs.js. The usual cause is being interrupted during shutdown by either an antivirus or VPN. Sometimes the file is read-only, in which case it's easy to fix. If you look in profile and see multiple prefs files, such as prefs-1.js, prefs-2.js, etc. that is further indication that thunderbird fails when shutting down. Although not a permanent fix, you can often restore the desired setting by removing all prefs files except the one with highest number, and renaming it to prefs.js. Repairing the cause is trial-and-error, again, usually an antivirus or VPN setting. That's all I know.

content:
The only password that Thunderbird can be set to use for itself is one to protect your Saved Passwords. That's all done completely locally to your computer and no code is ever sent.

Do you really mean changing the password for your email provider's account? That password can only be changed on the providers web site. During that procedure they may send you a code, but if you don't currently have valid credentials, most providers will ask you for an alternate way to receive the code, usually another email address or a text message. If you suspect that a code is being sent to the alternate address but is not being received by Thunderbird, use THAT providers web mail to check. If you don't see it there, the fault lies with the sender.
